notes: Hook checked against case.json: String B is 2.40 km of 66 kV cable from B01 to the OSS; L2 reads 2.20 GΩ at 1 minute against the client's 1 GΩ criterion, so it passes its IR figure, and the fault is then found by the sheath, VLF, TDR and LIRA tests from the ends. Holds.

oneBreath: a long capacitor in layers (ABB 0.22 µF/km; notes p.1 layer list), made safe before and after every test (notes p.2-3), core resistance for the conductors, IR curve and VLF for the insulation, sheath test for the oversheath (notes p.1: each test checks one layer) all hold.

oneBreath corrected: 'the VLF withstand the insulation at low and full stress' understated VLF, which runs at 1.5 to 2.5 U0 (notes p.7), above working stress. Now 'at low stress and above its working stress'. Applied to topic.json.

TDR and LIRA as reflections at impedance changes turned into a distance is a fair simplification of both (TDR time x velocity / 2; LIRA reads the reflection ripple in the impedance spectrum and places a spot along the cable). 'One made-up 66 kV cable with one fault' matches the case file.
